extracted.intended_audience: researchers and prospective authors (and referees/editors) for the Annals of Applied Statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Information and pointers for authors, referees, and editors about the Annals of Applied Statistics: scope, editorial areas, and where to find submission/manuscript/referee/ethical guidelines. Primarily directs readers to more detailed pages (Submissions, Manuscript Preparation, Guidelines for Referees, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — applied papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annals of Applied Statistics is aimed at papers in the applied half of [statistical research's] range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published quarterly in both print and electronic form; the journal's goal is to provide a timely and unified forum for all areas of applied statistics. (The site points authors to the 'Submissions' page for a complete statement of the kind of papers appropriate for AOAS.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical editorial areas / topical fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific editorial coverage is organized by topical editors: e.g., social, political, and environmental sciences; causal inference, design, and policy; computational biology, bioinformatics, genetics, and genomics; machine learning and artificial intelligence; neuroscience, physical science, and engineering; medical science, electronic health records, and smart health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider whether their manuscript fits one of these topical areas when submitting; see the Editorial Board for the AOAS Editorial Panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Click 'Submissions' at left for a complete description of how to submit papers for publication, and a statement of the kind of papers appropriate for AOAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main submission procedures and detailed requirements are provided on the dedicated 'Submissions' page linked from this page; follow those instructions when preparing and submitting manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript Preparation (and Supplement Instructions) are listed as resources for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow the journal's manuscript preparation and supplement instructions (linked from this page) for format, style, and supplementary materials; consult the linked pages for detailed formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Referees are provided (linked) as part of the journal resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should consult the journal's Guidelines for Referees page for standards and expectations when reviewing submissions (the current page lists the link but the substantive guidance is on the linked page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Principles for Authors, Referees, Associate Editors and Editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical Principles for Authors, Referees, Associate Editors and Editors are listed among the journal resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants in the publication process (authors, referees, editors) are expected to adhere to the journal's ethical principles; the linked policy pages contain the detailed rules and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Board / AOAS Editorial Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: The page directs readers to 'Editorial Board' for the AOAS Editorial Panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about the editorial panel (which signals editorial expectations and areas of expertise) is available via the Editorial Board link and helps authors identify appropriate editorial contacts or topical fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Published quarterly in both print and electronic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal issues are produced quarterly; authors and readers should expect quarterly publication cycles and both print and electronic accessibility.
